headline: High: CrewAI’s default shared-memory, shell, browser, and filesystem access can cascade into unsafe actions when paired with a non-networked data engine.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host working directory and uses shared memory by default, so malicious content in files or outputs could steer its agents. RisingWave is non-networked and exposes no direct ingestion channel, so the pairwise bridge is indirect rather than automatic. Uncertainty about any hidden shared workspace pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF CrewAI agents read attacker-controlled files from the shared working directory
IF RisingWave outputs are copied into CrewAI prompts without sanitization
mitigations: Separate the working directories for the two systems
Disable automatic file ingestion in CrewAI prompts
Add a provenance tag to any copied RisingWave output
Use a read-only export step between systems
requires-engineering: add content filtering before CrewAI tool calls

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI handles API keys and can access the host filesystem, but RisingWave has no network egress and no data classes listed. The pair does not show a direct shared workspace or authenticated cloud principal, so leakage risk is limited and mostly depends on operator-created file sharing. The lack of evidence for sensitive data in RisingWave keeps this low.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in CrewAI’s working directory
IF RisingWave-derived data is manually copied into CrewAI prompts or logs
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared directory
Use separate OS users for each system
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
Restrict file permissions on the CrewAI workspace
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on copied artifacts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI can write the filesystem, execute shells, and spawn subprocesses; RisingWave is a data-engineering system with no declared write or concurrency controls in the profile. Because the pair may touch the same host resources through the CrewAI side, conflict is plausible, but the absence of explicit RisingWave write surfaces prevents a higher severity. Uncertainty is resolved upward to medium.
conditions: IF both systems are pointed at the same mutable directory or database
IF CrewAI subprocesses modify artifacts that RisingWave also reads or writes
mitigations: Assign disjoint storage paths
Run CrewAI in a container with a separate volume
Avoid concurrent writes to shared artifacts
Use file locks for any shared outputs
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI can generate tool outputs and act through subprocesses, while RisingWave is a data-engineering backend that may consume upstream artifacts. If CrewAI output is treated as authoritative by downstream automation, errors can propagate into durable data products or actions. The interaction is not directly documented, so uncertainty is escalated to high because the blast radius can be irreversible.
conditions: IF RisingWave ingests CrewAI-produced artifacts without validation
IF downstream jobs materialize or publish data based on CrewAI output
mitigations: Insert a human review step before ingestion
Validate schemas and checksums on all CrewAI outputs
Mark CrewAI outputs as untrusted by default
Limit downstream jobs to dry-run mode first
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI explicitly handles API keys and developer-passed crew data, while RisingWave’s profile shows no data classes or residency commitments. There is no documented compliance mismatch between the pair, but CrewAI’s handling of secrets means any shared sensitive data needs operator review. Because RisingWave is not shown to process regulated data, this remains low.
conditions: IF regulated data is passed into CrewAI’s crew context
IF RisingWave stores or exports the same regulated data class
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of CrewAI prompts
Document data residency for any shared dataset
Review retention settings before enabling logging
Use separate storage for regulated and non-regulated data
requires-engineering: add compliance policy enforcement
